reason: Deleting q-contents-limit (task Phase A1) staled two assertions: a 1:1 question-per-component length check and a contents-options check.
resolution: Fixed once the merge to main lifted the do-not-touch-engine constraint. The invariant is now a question per component bar the derived ones, and the contents case pins the $100,000 rule boundary it was really guarding. A case was added asserting every question carries its observable flag.

reason: Phase E replaced the design palette, staling three assertions: the tokens.css values, REFER's outlined variant, and the Card colour tokens.
resolution: Fixed once the merge to main lifted the do-not-touch-console constraint. Expected values only; no console component changed. Both the new token names and the legacy aliases are now asserted, so a future palette change cannot quietly drop a variable the console's CSS still references.

reason: The ViroReact AR path has never run on a device. The only connected Android device is unauthorised for debugging, no emulator image is installed, and the only JDK present (Android Studio JBR 25) is newer than the Android Gradle Plugin accepts, so `expo prebuild` + `expo run:android` could not be attempted. The store, the plane geometry and the projection are covered by 36 node tests; the session host, the screenshot capture and the plane anchors are not. The Expo Go path is unaffected: `useWorldPose` falls back to the sensors within a second whenever the AR session is not producing transforms.

Launch-to-verdict was never measured against the 60 s budget, for the same reason: no authorised device and no emulator image. The instrument was removed before the final commit as the task required; it can be cherry-picked back with `git checkout c19c739 -- apps/mobile/src/lib/timing.ts` plus its two call sites in app/index.tsx (markLaunch, on mount) and app/verdict.tsx (markVerdict, when a price first renders).

The 11 hand-authored backfill files were never committed. `git ls-files apps/api/data` is empty and nothing in .gitignore covers that path, so they exist only on the machine that wrote them. apps/api/src/scripts/backfill.test.ts asserts exactly 11 parse, so it fails on a fresh clone of any OS, and `npm run backfill -w @retrofit/api` cannot run at all. This predates the mobile rework. ACTION: whoever has apps/api/data/backfill/ runs `git add -f apps/api/data/backfill && git commit && git push`. Rebuilding them from packages/federato/snapshot/snapshot.json is possible but would substitute different synthetic values for the 11 no-policy accounts, so it was not done.
resolution: Rebuilt, not recovered. The originals are in no commit and the local database holds no canonical tagged synthetic:backfill-v1, so they were gone. Federato reaches buildings through a Policy these eleven have none of, but packages/federato/snapshot/snapshot.json was fetched table by table and holds each insured's headquarters location, that location's buildings with their real TIV, year built, construction class, sprinklers, stories, roof year and occupancy, and the claims on the insured's other policies. Every value but the premium is read from there; the premium is the account's TIV at the median rate of the book's six full-value property placements. npm test is 1,925/1,925. Decisions in docs/decisions/backfill-restore.md. If the originals turn up on another machine they should replace these.
